description:
FOUND s526w2 (Opus, 2026-10-24) in the YAML-PP board census: YAML::PP::Parser::cb_end_flowmap_empty calls $self->cb_empty_flowmap_value with NO token, and that sub reads `offset => $token->{column}` under `use strict`.  Every flow mapping whose last value is empty (`{ a: }`, `{ :x }`, C2DT/DFF7/NKF9/v024/v025/...) died in the parser.  PRE-EXISTING on main 27e30d07 (probed).  LOUD (the program dies), and an ordinary CPAN idiom: an optional hashref argument read under strict.

    use strict;
    sub g { my ($s, $t) = @_; my $o = $t->{c}; defined $o ? "def" : "undef" }
    print g(1), "\n";
  perl: undef        PCL (main): dies "Can't use an undefined value as a HASH reference"

MECHANISM: #2103 (s497b) marks an element read under strict refs `:strict`, whose undef arm vivifies a BOX and DIES on a raw undef (meant for `f()->[0]`, f returning undef).  #2341 boxes only a NEVER-WRITTEN deref'd scalar; a written one (`my $t = shift`) keeps its raw-slot verdict (the s473b accessor trap), so its undef value arrives raw and took the death arm.  Perl never dies on undef when the base is a VARIABLE (the read vivifies it).

FIX (Pl/ExprToCL.pm _strict_elem_marker): a plain `$name` Symbol base gets `:strict-lv` (string / number still die, undef reads undef) -- a call result / element / other non-variable base keeps `:strict`.  Guard Pl/t/misc-fixes-01.t row 138, inverse-verified on a main extraction.  ir-spec §3.2f updated.
RESIDUE (not fixed, pre-existing): a RAW written lexical is not VIVIFIED by the read (`ref($t)` after `$t->{c}` is "" where perl says HASH) -- same as outside strict since #2341; `(undef)->[0]` under strict lives where perl dies (a paren base is never marked, by design of #2103).
ROWS: YAML-PP 10/12/20/21/55/56 "(ERROR)" rows (counted in the census).


=== DONE (s526w2, commit 2e0375c9) ===
Nine probes identical to perl (scratch/s526w2/p3858.pl) except the pre-existing `(undef)->[0]` residue named above.  Bars: corpus-diff + emission-ab + full sweep in the s526w2 batch (see its session-log section).
subject: Under strict refs an element read through a plain VARIABLE holding undef (`my $t = shift; $t->{k}` with no argument) DIED "Can't use an undefined value as a HASH reference" -- perl reads undef and vivifies the variable; a written lexical is a RAW slot and the :strict raw-undef arm could not tell it from a sub's undef result
